title: Affine neighbourhoods of finite sets in a Néron lft-group
statement: Let $D$ be a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one, $K=\operatorname{Frac}D$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $V/K$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite type, and let $N/S$ be a Néron lft-model of $V$ [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Thus $N$ is a smooth separated commutative $S$-group scheme, with a specified generic-fibre group isomorphism $N_K\simeq V$ [def-pc-base-change], such that restriction is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_S(Y,N)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_K(Y_K,V)$ for every smooth $S$-scheme $Y$. A group scheme has multiplication, inverse and identity morphisms satisfying the group diagrams [def-sc-group-scheme]; separated means the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every finite subset $P\subseteq |N|$ there exists an affine open subscheme $U\subseteq N$ containing $P$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Here affine means isomorphic to the spectrum of a commutative ring. The group $N$ itself need not be quasi-compact.

source.place: BLR 10.1, proof of Proposition 4, printed p.291 (PDF p.297), first sentence; preceding discussion printed p.290 and 6.4 Theorem 1 for the affine-neighbourhood input. Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-neron-lft-neutral-affine-product-chart] the fibrewise neutral subgroup $H=N^0$ is open. Over each of its affine base neighbourhoods $B$, a surjection $U\times_BU\to H_B$ has affine source, so $H_B$ is quasi-compact: pull back any open cover and take a finite subcover. Finitely many such $B$ cover the quasi-compact $S$, hence $H$ is quasi-compact. It is locally of finite type, so finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. It is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes], separated by restriction of the closed diagonal, and its geometric fibres are connected by the definition of $N^0$.

source.place: 10.1 after Definition 1, printed p.290: finite type of the identity component from the affine product chart.

proof.text: Choose an affine open neighbourhood in $N$ of each point of $P$ and take their finite union $W$ (use $W=\varnothing$ for $P=\varnothing$). A finite union of quasi-compact spaces is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-sfb-neutral-action-finite-type-saturation] to $N,H,W$. It supplies a smooth separated finite-type open $X\subseteq N$ containing $P$, stable under $H$, whose geometric fibre components are $H$-orbits. This uses finite type of $H$, not of $N$.

source.place: 6.6 Theorem 2, open image and (a); 10.1 p.290; finite-type neutral saturation in the lft case.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dedekind-smooth-fibre-dense-affine] to $X\to S$. Its hypotheses are exactly the smooth separated finite-type properties just obtained over the prescribed affine Dedekind base. Obtain an affine open $A\subseteq X$ dense in every geometric fibre and an effective Cartier divisor $E$ with complement $A$.

source.place: 6.4 Lemma 4 and proof of Theorem 1, printed pp.155–156: construct the fibrewise dense affine open.

proof.text: Each nonempty geometric fibre component of $X$ meets $A$, by density, and is a single $H$-orbit by Step 2. Over an algebraically closed field choose a point in this intersection; transitivity carries it to any prescribed geometric point in that component. Thus $H\times_SA\to X$ is surjective on points. The smooth finite-type group $H$ has geometrically connected fibres, so [lem-sfb-dedekind-action-boundary-ampleness] gives an absolutely ample invertible module $\mathcal O_X(E)$.

source.place: 6.4 Proposition 2 and Lemma 3, printed pp.153–155: affine complement meets all neutral orbits.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-ample-finite-set-affine] on $X$ to $P$ and the ample module just obtained. It gives an affine open $U\subseteq X$ containing $P$. Since $X$ is open in $N$, $U$ is also an open subscheme of $N$, with the same scheme structure, by [def-weil-open-immersion]. This proves the assertion without asserting quasi-compactness of $N$.

proof_origin.place: BLR 10.1 p.290 and proof of Proposition 4 p.291, using 6.4 Proposition 2 and proof of Theorem 1; explicit neutral-saturation reduction makes the non-quasi-compact case precise. Primary scan read online; local PDF WANTED. Stacks 01ZY finishes.
